name: tidy-const-views
description: 0.0.9 plan M-3, WA-CLANGD-010: clang-tidy's misc-const-correctness says a variable holding a filter view, or a view over one, can be declared const, and adding it breaks the build, since such a view caches begin() and has no const one (UP-22). The project's .clangd turns on the check for everything (FastCheckFilter: None, without which clang-tidy leaves it out of a file that includes a standard library), and the file has two such variables and one int that is never changed: the server shows the int and not the views. T1 waits for clangd's diagnostics (a diagnostic-code-lines check alone can read the empty set mcppls publishes before clangd has built the file, as on a Windows runner); T2 then holds the lines exactly. The standard library is the semantic kit's libc++ on every platform; workaround-canaries holds the same file against clangd alone, with the host's.
